2.1.1 INTRODUCTION The living species are the product of millions of years of organic evolution on earth. During this period many species appeared and disappeared. We are familiar with only a few species which inhabit or visit our surroundings. Even a short look at the small number of species around us at once shows diversity of life. A rose appears different from a lotus; a dog appears different from a cat. This simple instance is just a glimpse of the vast variety that exists in entire living world. The varieties of living things found on the earth are known as biodiversity or biological diversity. Biodiversity includes all the plants, animals, microorganisms and fungi. The study of varieties of plants from all sources is termed as floral diversity. It includes number of plants present, variation within and between species at the genetic level and role and function that plays in an ecosystem. 2.1.2 THREE DOMAINS OF LIFE ‘Domains’ are the top level classification that categorizes the life in the most general way. The three domain of life is a biological classification discovered by Carl Woese (1990). This classification system is also known as “Three Domains Classification” because it divides the life forms into three domains on the basis of differences of rRNA sequence. The domains of life are Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.
